headline: Ozona CCS and Marubeni reach FID on Texas's Pawnee carbon sequestration project
summary: The 50/50 Ozona-Marubeni JV took FID on the Pawnee project in Bee County, South Texas, capturing CO2 from a StarTex gas-treating facility and storing up to 400,000 t/yr in the Sligo Formation, with first injection targeted for Q1 2027. Marubeni leads carbon-credit marketing.
co2crc_note: Trading-house-backed (Marubeni) storage-plus-credit-marketing model mirrors the off-take/value-chain structures Australian CCS hubs are pursuing; a rare fresh FID data point.
extractor_note: FID date inferred from 24 Nov trade-coverage flurry and SPE announcement; per-article WebFetch date-verification blocked this session (all external hosts unresolvable).

headline: Malaysia: CCUS development should benefit all states, including Sabah and Sarawak, as national roadmap nears launch
summary: A federal minister said Malaysia's emerging CCUS industry must deliver value across all states, naming Sabah and Sarawak, as the government prepares to launch its Malaysia CCUS Roadmap 2050 by end-November, amid debate over federal-Sarawak regulatory coordination.
co2crc_note: Malaysia is an APAC CCS storage-hub competitor and prospective cross-border CO2 partner; the roadmap and federal/Sarawak split shape the regional market Australia operates in.

headline: CleanTechnica: COP31 plants a big wet kiss on failed carbon capture technology
summary: A sharply critical opinion piece argues the COP31 outcome lent undue legitimacy to CCS and carbon removal, framing the technology as a costly distraction from direct emissions cuts.
co2crc_note: Representative of the post-COP31 sceptic wave; relevant to CCS social-licence monitoring but no direct Australian/CO2CRC link.
